{{Quote|My life for yours.|Visas Marr, to Meetra Surik|<ref name="The Sith Lords" />}}
'''Visas Marr''' was a [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] from the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Katarr/Legends|Katarr]] who lived during the time of the [[Jedi Civil War]] and the [[Dark Wars|period of unrest]] that followed in its wake. In [[3952 BBY]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Atris]] held a [[Conclave at Katarr]] with the remaining Jedi from the [[First Jedi Purge]], whilst purposely leaking the event's whereabouts to the [[Sith Triumvirate]] and orchestrators of the Purge, in hopes of drawing them out. However, the plan backfired, and [[Darth Nihilus]], one of the Triumvirate's leaders, [[Force drain/Legends|consumed]] all organic life on the planet, striking a devastating blow to the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. However, Nihilus left Visas Marr alive on Katarr; she was taken aboard the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord's]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Ravager (Centurion-class)|''Ravager'']], and was made his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]]. Thus, a [[Force-bond/Legends|Force bond]] was forged between the two. Warped into a servant of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]], Marr later traveled with Nihilus beyond the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], before being dispatched in [[3951 BBY]] to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] to seek out a [[Meetra Surik|growing presence in the Force]] and bring its cause before Nihilus.

Marr found the center of the phenomenon she sought: a [[Meetra Surik|former Jedi]], exiled by the Order before Nihilus's rise to power, who had returned to known space. She ambushed and challenged the exiled Jedi, [[Meetra Surik]] who defeated Marr. Impressed by Surik's abilities and the destiny that she perceived about her, Marr allowed herself to be swayed to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]]. Forsaking her [[Sith Master/Legends|master]], Nihilus, she became an informal [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]] to Surik, teaching the elder ex-Jedi about the [[Force power/Legends|power]] of her [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Species/Legends|species]].

The Miraluka traveled with Surik and aided in her endeavor to save the Jedi Order by locating those [[Lost Jedi|Jedi Masters]] who had been absent from the convocation. Later that year, Marr played an instrumental part in resolving the [[Battle of Telos IV]], in which she met her former master in battle, and triumphed. In the process, she overcame the remaining shadows of her past, coming to terms with the destruction of her people. Soon afterward, Surik confronted and [[Battle of Malachor|defeated]] the two surviving members of the Triumvirate, [[Kreia|Darth Traya]] and [[Darth Sion]], at [[Malachor V]], ending the Sith's [[First Jedi Purge|program to eradicate]] the Jedi. Shortly before her death at the hands of Surik, Darth Traya prophesied of Marr's return to Katarr and her pivotal role in rebuilding the Jedi Order.

==Biography==
===Sith apprentice===
{{Quote|There are many kinds of hate, and all of them have the call of the dark side in them.|Visas Marr, to Meetra Surik|<ref name="The Sith Lords" />}}
In the year [[3952 BBY]], Visas Marr, a young [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]] [[Gender/Legends|female]], was living on her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] Miraluka colony of [[Katarr/Legends|Katarr]], when the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] was chosen to host a secret [[Conclave at Katarr|Jedi conclave]] to discuss the hidden dangers the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] had recently faced.<ref name="Jedi vs Sith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> [[3959 BBY|Seven years prior]], the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], a hero of the [[Mandalorian Wars]], had founded a new [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] and pronounced himself a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]. He, along with his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Darth Malak]], had [[Jedi Civil War|declared war]] on the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].

In the intervening years since the [[3956 BBY|conclusion]] of the war, the Jedi had been [[First Jedi Purge|disappearing]], hunted down one by one. The Miraluka, as a [[Species/Legends|species]], were innately [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], and the Jedi had hopes that the intensified [[The Force/Legends|Force]] energy on Katarr would provide them with a measure of clarity.<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> One of the leaders of the [[Sith Triumvirate]], [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Nihilus]], who possessed an [[Force drain/Legends|insatiable hunger]] for the Force, was drawn to Katarr by this gathering of those strong within it, from where he lurked beyond the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. Unable to ignore this emanating pulse of Force power, he consumed all life on the planet, wiping out the Jedi who had gathered there. Marr alone remained alive to bear witness.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" />

[[File:Visas.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Visas awakens aboard the [[Ravager (Centurion-class)|''Ravager'']].]]
Miraluka were typically made uneasy by the presence of something untouched by the Force, and when Marr not only saw, but experienced, the obliteration of life through the Force, the pain and shock of the severed connections left her unconscious and near [[Death/Legends|death]]. Taken aboard Nihilus's ship, she awoke to find that the flesh where her eyes would have been had been removed. Distraught, she sought out the Dark Lord, questioning why she alone had been spared.<ref name="Unseen, Unheard" /> Fractured and vulnerable at best, overwhelmed by the [[Sith sorcery/Legends|dark power]] surrounding him, Marr allowed Nihilus to take her for his own. In an attempt to make her believe in his cause, Nihilus showed her a vision, forcing her to ''see'' [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in a way that her people never could; sentient beings on other planets, disconnected from the life surrounding them, unable to feel the Force.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /><ref name="The Sith Lords" />

The vision severely damaged Marr's [[Force sight]]&mdash;which she, as a Miraluka, had to solely rely on, having no physical sight&mdash;and she became convinced that ''all'' life must die. She came to believe that Nihilus fed upon the ugliness of the galaxy and left silence, and that the removal of this wretchedness was bringing stillness and order to where there once had been chaos. Accepting Nihilus's unspoken invitation, Marr became his apprentice, and was given a meditation chamber, in addition to living quarters&mdash;which she called her cell&mdash;aboard the ''Ravager''. As Nihilus's [[Shadow Hand]],<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /> Marr was compelled to do her master's bidding. About one year later, she felt a growing [[Disturbance in the Force/Legends|disturbance in the Force]]. Perceiving it as a faint echo rippling through the galaxy, she sought out her master to inform him of the phenomenon, only to find that he had felt it as well. Curious and perhaps uneasy with the discovery, Nihilus demanded to know if Marr was capable of tracing the origin of the anomaly. After confirming the possibility, he sent her to find and bring the source to him.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

===Finding the source===
{{Quote|Her presence here is a threat to us. To you. Do not underestimate her&hellip; or her loyalty.|Kreia, to Meetra Surik|<ref name="The Sith Lords" />}}
[[File:Visas_marr_2.jpg|thumb|180px|Visas Marr serving the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Nihilus]].]]
Marr's search for the origin of the echoes lead her to [[Meetra Surik]], a former [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] in the Mandalorian Wars who had lost her connection to the Force during the war's [[Battle of Malachor V|culminating battle]] at [[Malachor V]]. The general alone returned to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to answer to the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] and defend her actions in disobeying them by joining Revan in his crusade against the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] threat. As a result, she was exiled from the Jedi Order.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /> After roaming the Outer Rim for nearly a decade, Surik had returned to Republic space and was being hunted by [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassins]] who believed her to be the last Jedi Knight. In an effort to save the Jedi Order, Surik set out on a mission to find the [[Lost Jedi|Jedi Masters]] that had not been present at the conclave on Katarr. During her journey, Surik experienced a burgeoning reconnection to the Force and any subsequent decisions she made sent tremors throughout the Force, thus allowing Marr to find her.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

{{GameLSmechanics|Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords}}
Marr infiltrated Surik's [[Starship/Legends|starship]], the ''[[Ebon Hawk]]'', incapacitated the crew, and [[Duel on the Ebon Hawk|engaged]] Surik in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]&mdash;only to be defeated, wounded, and have her [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] broken. Convinced of Surik's superior strength, Marr yielded and begged Surik to end her life, for the alternative was death by her master's hand for her failure. When Surik refused, Marr pledged her life to her, seemingly abandoning Nihilus before losing consciousness. Surik then took the unconscious woman to the ship's medical bay. This act of mercy was met by surprise from Surik's companion, the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] of the ''Ebon Hawk'', [[Atton Rand]], who was uneasy in the presence of powerful Force users, as the Miraluka were known to be. He also expressed his amazement at seeing a Miraluka [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], saying that he had heard of Miraluka Jedi, but never Sith, further speculating that he was unsure as to how to go about killing one. The idea of killing Marr was met by incredulity on the part of Surik, who voiced her regret for having hurt the Miraluka during their [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]]. Rand reassured her that Marr's injuries would heal, noticing that even though some of her wounds were severe, she looked like she had suffered from many more in the past.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

[[File:VisasChamberLight.jpg|thumb|left|240px|Visas comes to terms with her grief.]]
While Rand grudgingly accepted Marr, [[Kreia]], Surik's informal master, met her arrival with barely concealed contempt. She was of the opinion that the Miraluka's ability to see through the Force was wasted on her people and that she should be considered a servant. Furthermore, Kreia felt it necessary to remind Surik that the Sith were often betrayed by their own apprentices and that even though Marr had pledged herself to Surik, she was [[Force-bond/Legends|bound]] to other masters, thus insinuating that Marr's loyalty would always be suspect. Wary of Kreia's attitude towards Marr, Surik nonetheless sought her advice regarding the change Marr had brought about in her eyesight during their clash. While Kreia explained this alteration of Surik's perception was nothing that hadn't already been present, the elder woman had nothing but utter disdain for the forceful and "crude methods" that were the mark of the Sith.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

Marr's first genuine encounter with Surik left her disquieted. Unused to the mercy shown by Surik not only toward her, but others as well, Marr believed that this type of action would weaken Surik for the enemies she had to face in the near future. Nevertheless, impressed by Surik's skills, Marr rediscovered hope and came to consider that the universe was perhaps not as her master had shown her, and that, with her help, Surik would be able to stop him. The fact that her master neither understood nor ''saw'' Surik as she did was of some comfort to her. However, Marr cautioned Surik that she would need to understand why this was so if Surik was to have a chance of defeating Nihilus. She refused to guide Surik to him untested and without her potential realized, as Marr felt the Jedi was not yet ready to face such a threat. She foresaw that Surik and Nihilus would meet in the near future, however.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

===Journeys with Meetra Surik===
{{Quote|[&hellip;] but please, do not harm her&hellip; do not what you did to me&hellip; I beg you.|Visas Marr, to Darth Nihilus, during a confrontation on the ''Ravager''|<ref name="The Sith Lords" />}}
[[File:Normal_Visas-Marr-22.jpg|thumb|right|170px|Visas Marr during her travel with Meetra Surik.]]
From that moment, Marr devoted herself to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] and to the search for the remaining Jedi Masters. Her admiration for Surik continued to grow, and from her Surik would learn to see through the Force as a Miraluka could. When the time came for Surik to finally confront Marr's former master aboard his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Ravager (Centurion-class)|''Ravager'']], following [[Battle of Telos IV|his assault]] on the planet [[Telos IV]], Marr refused to be left behind, intuiting that her presence would be essential in vanquishing Nihilus.<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> Likewise, [[Canderous Ordo|Mandalore the Preserver]], who had been traveling with Surik in order to gather the scattered Mandalorian [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|clans]], insisted that he and his [[Mandalorians (Clan Ordo)|troops]] lead the charge into battle, claiming that his warriors were the most capable for the task.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /><ref name="The Sith Lords" />

Arriving on the ruined ship, Mandalore announced that he would be accompanying Marr and Surik to the bridge, asserting that he didn't trust Surik to complete the mission.<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> However, his low opinion of Surik's capabilities was not so much directed towards her specifically, as it was a general belief that anyone who was not a Mandalorian was ineffective.<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> As they made their way to the bridge, Marr, with Surik's blessing, took the time to visit her meditation chamber on the vessel one last time, finally coming to terms with the destruction of Katarr. Her new-found strength would see Marr through the trial ahead, not for vengeance but for the sake of all life. In a final test of allegiance, Marr confronted Darth Nihilus with her fate resting solely on Surik, who gave her the chance to stand up to the one who had wounded her.<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> As they were taken aback by the Sith Lord's powers, Nihilus stunned Surik and Marr offered her life in exchange for sparing her. This show of devotion distracted Nihilus long enough for Surik to recover.<ref name="Nihilus CSWE">{{CSWECite|II||Nihilus, Darth}}</ref> Surik realized that Marr was a link between Nihilus and the power bound within the ''Ravager''. Struggling as she was with the weight of that power, Marr exploited the bond to her former master and blocked his connection to the Force, momentarily stunning him. Together, Mandalore, Marr, and Surik were able to defeat Nihilus. Before they could make haste to flee the destruction of the ship, Marr felt compelled to behold what lay beneath [[Mask of Darth Nihilus|Nihilus's death mask]] in order to sever the last remaining bond between them.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

Soon after the death of Darth Nihilus, Surik confronted and [[Battle of Malachor|defeated]] the last two leaders of the Sith Triumvirate, [[Darth Sion]] and Surik's former teacher, Kreia, who had re-assumed the title of Darth Traya. This last struggle took place at the Triumvirate's headquarters, the ancient [[Trayus Academy]], located within the depths of Malachor V's craggy surface. This final battle brought about the end of the [[Dark Wars|shadow conflict]] that the Jedi had faced since the end of the Jedi Civil War, and Marr would play a role in the subsequent restoration of the Jedi Order.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /> Furthermore, according to Darth Traya's final predictions shortly before her death, Marr returned to her homeworld and, looking upon its surface, finally saw what she was meant to see.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Visas_sockets.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Visas with her eye sockets undamaged]]
The Miraluka were acknowledged as individuals strongly committed to their chosen course of action, as was evidenced by Marr's dedication to help Meetra Surik in stopping her former master.<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> Nevertheless, the trauma of seeing her world die through the Force left Marr shattered and vulnerable, her Force Sight damaged. Darth Nihilus took advantage of this and twisted her psyche until she became utterly subservient and hopeless, disconnected from herself and life, a mere shell of a being.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" />

Marr's defeat at the hands of Surik proved to be the catalyst that allowed her to break Nihilus's hold over her and restore her own free will. She confessed to Surik that the very fact that Surik's nature had eluded her master gave her hope that he could be defeated. The search for the Jedi Masters reestablished Marr's connection to life and believing Surik responsible for this, she vowed to protect her. Although she never quite lost her servile attitude, Marr's journey with Surik allowed her to gain the confidence and self-respect that ultimately severed the final bond to her former master and enabled her to rediscover herself.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

==Powers and abilities==
[[File:Visas_and_HK.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Visas attacking an [[HK-series assassin droid]]]]
Like all of her species, the Miraluka, Marr was born physically blind and instead relied on [[Force sight]] to ''see'' the physical world,<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /> which included the ability to see through walls.<ref name="Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''</ref> Though this [[Force power/Legends|Force power]] was a characteristic of the Miraluka, it was not species restrictive and Marr would later teach its use to Meetra Surik.<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> Her [[Force sense/Legends|sense of the Force]] was highly developed, as was evidenced by her detection of Surik, from across the galaxy, during her time as apprentice to Darth Nihilus.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /><ref name="PrimaK2" /> The depth of her Force-sensitivity granted Marr the ability to manipulate the Force to move or control the direction of objects through space. This was commonly known as the "Jedi's object movement power," also referred to as [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]].<ref name="Jedi vs Sith" /> The use of this talent included pulling and pushing objects with minimal effort.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /><ref name="Roleplaying Rulebook">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref> In addition, she may also have been a practitioner of [[Farsight/Legends|farsight]], as she was able to 'see' the eventual showdown between her first and her final master.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

Furthermore, Marr was highly skilled in the use of what were considered to be [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] powers, such as grasping and choking enemies, as well as unleashing [[Force lightning/Legends|raw dark-side energy]].<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> Her connection to the dark side gave her the use of Dark Healing,<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /> an ability that fueled regenerative processes by draining the life force of another.<ref name="Roleplaying Rulebook" /> Marr's return to the light side following her defeat at the hands of Meetra Surik allowed her to continue training as a [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|Jedi Sentinel]]. Because of her training as a Jedi Sentinel, she was later given a yellow-bladed lightsaber by Surik,<ref name="PrimaK2" /> which served to extend her knowledge of lightsaber combat.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

==Behind the scenes==
Visas Marr was created by [[Obsidian Entertainment]] as one of the companions for the [[2004]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''. Like most companions, she was written by [[Chris Avellone]].<ref name="15 Years">{{WebCite|url=http://www.cinelinx.com/news/culture/knights-of-the-old-republic-ii-developer-chris-avellone-discusses-the-games-impact-15-years-later|text=Knights of the Old Republic II Developer Chris Avellone Discusses the Game's Impact 15 Years Later|work=[https://www.cinelinx.com Cinelinx]|archivedate=20191208220416|author=Maison, Jordan|date=2019-12-06|quote=I had to write almost all the companions, except for Mandalore and Bao-Dur (who was written by Michael Chu[)]}}</ref> She was voiced by American actress [[Kelly Hu]].<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> One of her co-creators was concept artist [[Brian Menze]].<ref name="Menze">{{DeviantArt|username=brenze|url=comments/1/147113336/1705902953|name=[[Brian Menze]]|text=Comment on Visas Marr by Brenze}}</ref> Marr's story and background was later elaborated in the six-page comic "[[Unseen, Unheard]]," which was featured in [[Star Wars Tales 24|''Star Wars Tales'' 24]], and the ''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''. In addition, the Jedi Sentinel miniature in [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[Champions of the Force (Star Wars Miniatures)|''Champions of the Force'']] miniatures set resembles Visas Marr.<ref name="WizardsCite-''Champions of the Force'' Preview 7">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/CotFPreview7|text=''Champions of the Force'' Preview 7}}</ref> A second miniature, this one explicitly labeled as being Marr, was released in the [[Knights of the Old Republic (Star Wars Miniatures)|''Knights of the Old Republic'']] set.<ref>{{Wizards|url=swminis/swminis_autocard.asp?id=visas_marr&set=KOTOR|text=Star Wars Miniatures: Visas Marr|nobackup=1}} URL accessed on 13 February 2010.</ref>

At one point, there was some confusion as to Marr's actions aboard the ''Ravager'' and her involvement in the death of Darth Nihilus. [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']], written as an [[in-universe]] historical account, claimed that it was unclear as to whether Marr had killed Nihilus, moreover implying that Nihilus may have in fact killed her.<ref name="Jedi vs Sith" /> The matter appeared to be settled in ''Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide'', where it was stated that Marr led Surik to her former master and that afterward she was pivotal in the restoration of the Jedi Order.<ref name="KOTOR campaign guide" /> In addition, the player had the option to convince Marr to sacrifice herself for the purpose of weakening Nihilus, but only if Marr was equipped with standard clothes and wielded a melee weapon or a lightsaber.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'': Conversation option with Visas part-way through the duel with Nihilus: "You are his weakness&mdash;and you must be sacrificed if I am to live."</ref>

[[File:Visasconcept.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Concept art of Visas Marr]]
The game mechanics of ''Knights of the Old Republic II'' enabled a player to choose to play either a light side or dark side character. Depending on the chosen path, the dialog choices between the player and the companions was altered, in addition to the monologues of the companions themselves. Furthermore, the alignment choices led to a change in the side quests available to the player, as well as certain action sequences of the game. An example of gameplay changes with regards to Visas Marr was if Surik chose the path of the dark side; Marr slowly forgot about Katarr and instead gained an unstoppable vengeance against anyone that had ever hurt her physically or emotionally. Additionally, Marr's experience in her meditation chamber aboard the ''Ravager'' was altered. If Surik followed the light path, Marr heard whispers; if Surik followed the dark side path, Marr heard screams.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

In order for the player to gain a prestige class&mdash;the equivalent of a Jedi Master&mdash;in ''Knights of the Old Republic II'', the functions of game mechanics required Marr to become a companion of Surik as a prerequisite. Furthermore, Marr was one of two females who would refuse to dance for [[Vogga]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] in the player quest "Vogga's Dancers." The other female was Kreia.<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> There was also an item called "Visas Marr's lightsaber" that could have been obtained by using a cheat code, however, it was unclear as to whether this was the same lightsaber Marr carried when she first infiltrated the ''Ebon Hawk''. This item was a slightly more efficient [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|red]]-bladed lightsaber with no special features other than Marr's name on it.<ref name="TLK Saber">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'':'' Dialog.tlk file StrRefs 131363 and 131364</ref>

===Romance===
{{Quote|From the moment I heard your voice across the galaxy, I have longed for you&mdash;When I heard it, I loved you more than my own life. And I wanted you to be here with me, for as long as you will let me love you.|Visas Marr, to a male Jedi Exile|<ref name="The Sith Lords" />}}
The publication of ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'' established the [[canon]]icity of Meetra Surik as being of the female sex. As a result of game mechanics, a player had the option to play as either a male or female character. If the player chose a male character, Marr, along with the male-player-only character [[Brianna]], was intended to be one of two romantic interests that could be chosen. Technically, however, it was not possible to have a romance with either one. Unlike the first [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic|''Knights of the Old Republic'']] game, there wasn't a dialog-driven romance progression. Much of the romance was alluded to in the form of conversations between characters and cutscenes. It was only toward the end of the game that Marr confessed her love for the male Surik as long as he had gained enough influence with her, although the player character did not have the option of returning those feelings.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

Marr and Brianna viewed themselves as rivals for the affections of Surik. They had a cutscene together in which Brianna jealously confronted Marr, claiming that she would only bring him harm. Marr's response was to state that she only wanted to protect Surik and that Brianna was aware of this since she had read as much in Marr's movements, much the same as Marr had seen in Brianna's movements. Marr then went on to ask Brianna to describe what Surik looked like, to which Brianna was unable to give a satisfactory answer, professing that he looked like a man, but also more than a man. Another cutscene centered around the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Mira]], another companion of Surik, and her inability to understand why Brianna and Marr were fighting over Surik. She was of the opinion that since she had caught him&mdash;Mira initially tracked Surik for [[Zez-Kai Ell]], one of the lost Jedi Masters Surik sought, on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]&mdash;he belonged to her.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

There were at least two occurrences of conversations focusing of the physical aspects of a romance between Surik and Marr. One was voiced aloud by Kreia soon after Marr joined the group aboard the ''Ebon Hawk''. She urged Surik to control his urges and avoid mating with the seer, as this would have had the potential to create both physical and emotional difficulties. The player had the option to reply in the negative, stating that sparing her life did not mean that he had a romantic interest in her. To this response Kreia was skeptical, replying that Surik should have learned restraint and discipline while in exile. Another occurred when, after initiating a conversation with Mira, Mira remarked that Surik seemed to have a strange peace. After telling Mira that his peace is through the Force, Mira said that she thought Surik and Visas might have "hooked up a power coupling". If Surik replies with confusion, Mira explains, "You know, been intimate." (''Note: This latter dialogue also occurs if the player's love interest is the Handmaiden.'')<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

After the death of the Jedi Masters at the Jedi Enclave and Surik's discovery that his ability to form very strong Force bonds was the reason his companions followed his lead, Marr confessed her love to him. She did not believe that the Masters were right; it was her choice to follow him, her choice to sacrifice herself for him if need be. She explained that ever since she first heard him through the Force she understood that there was someone who felt the same sense of loss as she and that she had loved him from that moment. She begged Surik to stay with her, even as she knew that he could not. Her final request to him was to have the opportunity to ''see'' him at a moment where they were alone. This led to them meditating together, looking at each other with Force Sight.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

===Cut content===
[[File:Visassacrifice.png|thumb|right|180px|Visas is able to sacrifice herself on board the ''Ravager''.]]
According to developer comments in the game's conversation file, another scene involved the initial battle between the player and Marr in which she used her Force Sight to blind the player.<ref name="TLK Blind">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'':'' Dialog.tlk file StrRef 103602</ref> In a scene related to the endgame, Marr confronted Kreia at the Jedi Enclave. Kreia once again expressed her loathing of the Miraluka and berated her weak character.<ref name="Enclave">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'':'' Dialog.tlk file StrRefs 111564-111573</ref>
